text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 3.26% today as oil prices stabilized amid conflicting supply signals—Russian diesel potentially entering markets could ease fuel costs, but Middle Eastern tensions (Saudi attacks, Iran nuclear fortification, ongoing Houthi strikes) continue to threaten regional supply. U.S. refineries are running at 92.7% capacity with crude inventories at comfortable levels, so the refiner is well-positioned to profit if global oil prices remain elevated while domestic fuel supplies stay ample.

The stock's 20.85% surge over two weeks reflects a broader tailwind for refiners: Brent crude topped $106 just yesterday on geopolitical risk, and the wide gap between world oil ($125.44/barrel) and U.S. oil ($96.24/barrel) creates favorable margins for companies that process crude and sell refined products into global markets. Even if Trump's Russian diesel deal materializes, it represents only two weeks of U.S. demand, so supply concerns aren't disappearing anytime soon.
